corpus_crossquery.query: Do CLAIM 009 (mitochondrial/redox, in observation) or CLAIM 034 (counter-direction) already carry a ROS-rescue result for a Wwox-null system?
corpus_crossquery.finding: Both claims exist and neither carries this one. The NAC rescue in Wwox-null MEFs is adjacent to CLAIM 009's redox axis and does not resolve its tension with CLAIM 034, because it is a fibroblast culture result with no neural or in vivo arm. Logged as a lead in the analysis note, not proposed as a claim.

entries.proposition: Figure 1d quantifies gamma-H2AX-positive cells against the heterozygote, not wild type. Hand-read bar heights: early passage about 4.5 % (het) versus about 7.5 % (null), marked N.S.; late passage (passages 20-30) about 20.5 % versus about 35.5 %, marked ***. The loss-side rise is therefore conditional on long serial culture: it is not significant at early passage, and passage alone raises the heterozygote about 4.6-fold (20.5/4.5) while genotype at late passage adds about 1.7-fold (35.5/20.5).

entries.proposition: Figure 6c, 6g (hand readings, panel g enlarged 3x): SA-beta-gal-positive cells in late passage are about 35% (+/+), 17% (+/-), 1.5% (-/-) and 35% (-/- with 1 mM NAC). In panel g, p16 and p21 are absent or faint in late -/- and restored with NAC, p53 is reduced and restored, and WWOX stays absent in the NAC lane. The comparator of panel g is the heterozygote; no +/+ lane. NAC restores the CDK-inhibitor and senescence phenotype downstream of, or independent of, WWOX, which is what the Discussion's ROS claim rests on, without an ROS re-measurement. The wild type itself is 35% senescent at that passage.

entries.proposition: Figures 4 and 5: the p53 point mutations (A135P, V213G in the DNA-binding domain) were found in one late-passage null clone (no. 56) and in no other clone; the same clone shows large nuclear p53, Ser18 phosphorylation and no p21 induction, whereas the other null clones show low p53. Ectopic wild-type p53 restores p21, growth suppression and SA-beta-gal (about 20%) in clone 56. No panel sequences p53 in NAC-treated cells, so the 'ROS causes p53 mutations' step is an inference from one clone, not a tested link.

entries.proposition: Figure 3 (hand readings): the p16 promoter-luciferase signal is about 1.5-fold HIGHER in null than heterozygote while p16 protein is absent, i.e. the loss is post-transcriptional or epigenetic (the paper's methylation arm); the p21 reporter is about 0.15-fold. Re-expression of p16, p21 or both restores SA-beta-gal (about 15% versus 5%) and suppresses growth in null cells with no WWOX present (WWOX blot lane empty). The senescence phenotype is rescued downstream of WWOX, not by WWOX re-expression.

entries.proposition: Supplementary Figure 8 is a 16-row Agilent heatmap (Cyp1a1, G6pdx, Gstp1, Mpo, Nfe2l2, Nos3, Nqo1, Park2, Prdx4, Sod3, Trim30a; two probes for five genes) of early-passage Wwox-/- versus Wwox+/- MEFs, all rows red (higher in null), colour scale about -1 to +1 log2, one column per genotype, no replicate count and no statistics; the selection of genes is not explained. It supports an early redox-gene signature in the null while Figure 6a shows no early-passage ROS difference: the redox transcript change precedes the measured ROS change. G6pdx (pentose phosphate pathway) and Nfe2l2/Nqo1 are the only metabolic or NRF2-axis genes.
